title: Huang out as Nvidia CEO, SEC probe reported
since_label: Fri 6 Nov close, the last price before the weekend reports
status: Kalshi News and The Motley Fool report Nvidia shares fell 12% to 14% on Fri 20 Nov after Reuters reported the SEC is looking into the company's accounting practices, leaving the stock 47% below its 52-week high, and Kalshi News says Trump again called for Huang's return. GeekWire reports board chair Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate Huang, and the WSJ and Bloomberg report Heidrick & Struggles has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas; no permanent CEO has been named and the scope of the SEC inquiry is still open.
why: Nvidia is the anchor of the AI trade and one of the heaviest weights in the Nasdaq, which alts follow.
next_label: House committees' closed-door interview with Huang
sources: Reuters, Kalshi News, The Motley Fool, GeekWire, WSJ, Bloomberg, CNN, CNBC

title: Anthropic IPO, the largest AI listing
since_label: Tue 10 Nov, when the price range was set
status: Yahoo Finance and Seeking Alpha report ANT closed Fri 20 Nov at $88.91, down 8.5% from its $97.17 debut close, after trading as low as $83.05, just above the $83 IPO price, and Yahoo puts the market value at about $1.19T. BitcoinWorld says the post-IPO slide added to pressure on crypto; whether the stock holds its IPO price when trading resumes on Monday is still open.
why: A raise this size absorbs cash that would otherwise chase other risk, and its first-day close reprices every AI name.
sources: Yahoo Finance, Seeking Alpha, Morningstar, CNN, CNBC, Bloomberg, BitcoinWorld

title: Iran and US trade strikes in the Gulf
since_label: Thu 12 Nov 00:00 UTC, before Iran reported the Sirik strike
status: Arab Times reports Iran's deputy parliament speaker said on Sat 21 Nov that oil tankers are already moving to break the US blockade and that a lawmaker put the number preparing at 14, and Maritime Executive quotes Foreign Minister Araghchi saying the blockade must be broken. AGBI, citing Windward, reports no Iran-linked tankers were seen heading for Hormuz as of 19 Nov, and ABC News reports attacks in the strait are at their highest level of the war; no convoy sailing and no ceasefire has been confirmed.
why: CoinDesk cites the Gulf escalation, with the dollar and Fed hike odds, behind the crypto sell-off; oil feeds straight into rate expectations.
sources: Arab Times, Maritime Executive, AGBI, ABC News, Al Jazeera, Iran International, RFE/RL, CoinDesk

title: MSCI drops Strategy from its indexes
since_label: Wed 11 Nov close, before MSCI's after-hours announcement
status: Crypto Times reports Strategy fell 8.5% as bitcoin slid below $59,000, with about $541M pulled from BlackRock's IBIT in a single day, and CoinGlass data show bitcoin touched about $55,127 on Sat 21 Nov, which Crypto Times calls its lowest level in more than two years. MSCI's deletion takes effect after the close on 30 Nov, with BitcoinWorld estimating $2B to $3B of passive selling; whether other index providers follow is still open.
why: Strategy is the largest corporate BTC holder, and forced selling of its shares tests the main route equity money takes into bitcoin.
sources: MSCI, Strategy, Crypto Times, CoinGlass, BitcoinWorld, Bitcoin Magazine, CoinDesk, Decrypt

title: Binance $6.3B hack, stolen ETH on the move
since_label: Thu 29 Oct 00:00 UTC, before the hack was reported
status: Elliptic reports the hackers moved about 488,000 ETH, worth about $860M, out of their largest wallets from 17 to 20 Nov and have swapped about 39,000 ETH into roughly 1,100 BTC through THORChain, and Cointelegraph, citing Arkham, says about 224,700 ETH remain in the tracked addresses. Binance says it has replenished affected assets and about 44% of the stolen funds have been frozen or seized; an Abu Dhabi hearing on 1 Dec will decide whether 18 firms must hand over the assets they have frozen.
why: Stolen ETH that no issuer can freeze is being moved and swapped, a supply overhang for ETH and alts while crypto sentiment sits at extreme fear.
next_label: Abu Dhabi court hearing on frozen assets
sources: Binance, Elliptic, Cointelegraph, Reuters, Crypto Times, CoinDesk
